name: Tips, lists and dad life
notes: Ten slideshows: three single tips (the start of a numbered series), three funny ones (two about parenting with POTS), a word-only one, two that go for the heart, and a morning routine. Every one ends on the app.

creatives.name: Tip 1: water before you stand
creatives.title: POTS tip #1: water and electrolytes before your feet hit the floor 💧
creatives.goal: First of a numbered single-tip series. Save-worthy, one idea only.
creatives.caption: POTS tip #1. One tip at a time, because nobody with brain fog needs a list of 30 🩵 Not medical advice, ask your doctor what's right for you. #pots #potstips #dysautonomia #chronicillness #spoonie

text: POTS tip #1:
Drink *16 oz of water* before your feet hit the floor.
Preferably with electrolytes in it. 🧂:awesome:

img.shows: A wooden spoon heaped with coarse salt on a near-black surface, a few grains scattered around it, shot from above.
img.frame: Spoon in the lower half, centred; the tip sits in the dark space above it.
img.credit: Unsplash photo 1518110925495-5fe2fda0442c (photographer not looked up yet)

text: I set it out before bed so it is *ready when I wake up.*
Electrolytes help boost blood volume, which *steadies your blood pressure* when you stand.
slides.fine: Not medical advice. Ask your doctor about fluids and salt.

img.shows: A hand reaching for a water bottle from bed, sheets in the frame. No face.
img.frame: Hand and bottle in the top half; the copy covers the darkened bottom.

text: I log it so I can see *how fluids impact my POTS.*
Free app I built, link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Water sheet: 0.5 L, 2 cups, the first two glasses filled in blue, goal 3 L a day.
img.frame: Full-height screenshot; the two filled glasses sit beside the copy.

music.notes: Soft, bright and unhurried, like the first ten minutes of a day. Nothing dramatic: a tip should feel like a friend telling you something, not an ad. Pick something you would be happy to reuse on every tip in the series so they are recognisable.

creatives.title: The POTS dictionary, volume 1 📖
creatives.goal: Funny and shareable. People tag the friend who gets it.
creatives.caption: Words you only learn the hard way 🩵 What would you add to volume 2? #pots #dysautonomia #chronicillnesshumor #spoonie #longcovid

text: The POTS dictionary.
*Words I never wanted to learn.*

img.shows: An open dictionary page shot at an angle, shallow focus, the sharp entries on the right.
img.frame: The in-focus column behind the headline; darkened so the print reads as texture.
img.credit: Unsplash photo 1583361704493-d4d4d1b1d70a (photographer not looked up yet)

text: Preload: chugging water before attempting to be a person
Spoons: energy, but you only get 12
Coat hanger pain: your neck filing a complaint
Presyncope: the room carries on without you
Pacing: quitting while you're ahead, on purpose

img.shows: Plain white paper with a fine grain.
img.frame: Texture only, behind the list.
img.credit: Unsplash photo 1604147706283-d7119b5b822c (photographer not looked up yet)

text: I track all of them, so I *know what helps and what hurts.*
Free app I built, link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal's Symptoms list (light headed, palpitations, fatigue, brain fog), Triggers and Hydration.
img.frame: Symptoms card beside the copy.

music.notes: Something with a wink: plucky strings, a bouncy bass line or a quirky comedy bed. It should make the list read as jokes, so keep it light and steady with no vocals over the list slide.

creatives.name: Things my kids think are normal
creatives.title: Things my kids think are normal because Dad has POTS 😂
creatives.goal: Parenting humour. The POTSDad voice at its most itself.
creatives.caption: They have never once questioned why Dad is on the floor 😂🩵 Chronically ill parents, what's yours? #pots #potsdad #chronicillnessparent #dysautonomia #dadlife

text: Things my kids think are *totally normal* because their dad has POTS.

img.shows: You lying flat on the living room or kitchen floor, toys around you, looking at the camera like this is a regular Tuesday.
img.frame: Shot from above or from kid height. Your face in the upper third; the hook goes across the middle.

text: 1. Dad lying on the kitchen floor
2. Salt on everything
3. "Is your heart doing the thing?"
4. Hide and seek where Dad always hides lying down
5. The couch is base camp

img.shows: Kids' toys scattered on a living room floor. No people.
img.frame: Darkened about 85% under the list.

text: I track my numbers so I know which days are *floor days.*
Free app I built, link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home: the Outlook card with the Autonomic score (96), the pacing strip and key figures, giveaway card below.
img.frame: Full-height screenshot from the top.

music.notes: A sitcom-ish feel-good bed: ukulele, whistling, hand claps. The joke is affectionate, so nothing sarcastic or sad. A trending 'things my kids think are normal' style sound would work too.

creatives.name: To the parent on the bench
creatives.title: To the parent who had to sit down at the playground today
creatives.goal: Heart strings. Written to be sent to someone.
creatives.caption: If nobody told you today: showing up counts 🩵 Send this to a parent who needs it. #chronicillnessparent #pots #dysautonomia #longcovid #potsdad

text: To the parent who had to *sit down* at the playground today.

img.shows: An empty bench at the edge of a playground, late afternoon light. No people.
img.frame: Bench in the lower half; the hook sits in the sky or trees above it.

text: You didn't miss it.
You were *right there.*

img.shows: A child on a swing or slide seen from behind or far away, no face readable.
img.frame: Child in the top half, as if seen from the bench. Copy over the darkened lower half.

text: They won't remember that you sat.
They'll remember *that you came.*

img.search: parent child holding hands close up
img.shows: A small hand holding an adult's hand, close up. No faces.
img.frame: Hands in the upper third; copy underneath.

text: I pace my days so there's something left *for them.*
The app I built is in my bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home: Outlook card with the score, the pacing strip (1h 21m left of 3h 35m) and key figures.
img.frame: Full-height screenshot from the top; the pacing strip level with the copy.

music.mood: Tender piano, hopeful by the end
music.notes: Sparse and slow under the first slide, a little warmer with each one. It should land as kind rather than sad: the last slide is about having something left, so let it lift there. Instrumental only.

creatives.name: Tip 2: legs up the wall
creatives.title: POTS tip #2: put your legs up the wall for 10 minutes
creatives.goal: Second single tip. Something people can do tonight.
creatives.caption: POTS tip #2. Ten minutes, zero equipment 🩵 Not medical advice, ask your doctor what's right for you. #pots #potstips #dysautonomia #pacing #spoonie

text: POTS tip #2:
*Legs up the wall.* 10 minutes. That's the whole tip.

img.shows: Someone lying on the floor with their legs up a plain wall, shot from the side or showing legs only. No face.
img.frame: Legs and wall fill the frame; the tip sits over the darkened middle.

text: Gravity pulls blood into my legs all day.
For ten minutes, *I make it work for me.*
slides.fine: Not medical advice. Ask your doctor what's right for you.

img.shows: Feet in socks resting high on a wall, soft indoor light. No face.
img.frame: Feet in the top third; copy across the lower half.

text: In the app I built, resting like this *buys back time* on my pacing budget.
Link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home with the pacing strip (1h 21m left of 3h 35m). Better: a day with a legs-up entry logged, so the strip shows minutes bought back.
img.frame: Pacing strip level with the copy.

music.notes: Same sound family as tip #1 so the series is recognisable. Slow and restful: this one is about lying down.

creatives.name: Harder than cardio
creatives.title: Things that spike my heart rate more than a workout
creatives.goal: Funny list that doubles as awareness. Ends on proof.
creatives.caption: I am not out of shape, my nervous system is just dramatic 😅🩵 #pots #dysautonomia #chronicillnesshumor #longcovid #spoonie

text: Things that spike my heart rate *more than a workout.*

img.shows: A laundry basket half folded, sitting on a bed or couch. No people.
img.frame: Basket in the lower half, hook above it.

text: 1. Standing in line
2. A hot shower
3. Folding laundry
4. Tying a tiny shoe
5. The stairs. Just the stairs.

img.shows: A plain indoor staircase, looking up.
img.frame: Darkened about 85% under the list.

text: I'm not out of shape. *I have the receipts.*
Free app in bio to record yours. 🩵

img.shows: A POTS Test result: sustained HR rise +45 bpm (bad), the heart rate trace jumping at the stand, baseline 66, peak 118.
img.frame: The +45 and the trace beside the copy.

music.notes: The joke is the mismatch: gym-montage intensity over folding laundry. An over-the-top motivational or training beat, played straight. Drop to something softer on the last slide if the sound allows.

creatives.name: But you look fine
creatives.title: "But you look fine" 🙃
creatives.goal: Two slides, almost all words. Quick, quotable, shareable.
creatives.caption: Looking fine is a full-time job 🙃🩵 #pots #dysautonomia #chronicillness #longcovid #spoonie

text: "But you look fine."
Thanks. It took *2 liters of water, a lot of salt and a nap.*

img.shows: You looking perfectly fine: a polite, slightly tired smile straight at the camera.
img.frame: Face in the upper third. The deadpan is the joke, so don't oversell it.

text: What I look like and what my body is doing are *two different things.*
I track the second one. Free app in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home: Outlook card with the score, pacing strip, HRV / resting HR / sleep tiles.
img.frame: Full-height screenshot from the top.

music.notes: Two slides, so the sound does a lot of the work. A deadpan trending sound or a short awkward-pause comedy sting fits best.

creatives.name: What counts as a win now
creatives.title: What counts as a win when you're chronically ill
creatives.goal: Heart strings through a list. Gentle, a little proud.
creatives.caption: Old me would not understand this list. Current me is proud of every line 🩵 What was your win today? #pots #dysautonomia #chronicillness #longcovid #smallwins

text: The old me wouldn't believe *what I count as a win now.*

img.shows: You doing something small and ordinary: stirring a pot, tying a kid's shoe, standing at the door with a backpack.
img.frame: Candid, not posed. You in the upper half; the hook across the darkened middle.

text: 1. Showered standing up
2. Made dinner, and ate it too
3. Stood through school pickup
4. Read the bedtime story sitting up
5. Still had something left at 7pm

img.shows: Warm evening light falling on a plain wall or curtain.
img.frame: Darkened about 85% under the list.

text: I write them down so the bad days *can't erase them.*
Free app I built, link in bio. 🩵

img.frame: Raw full-height screenshot, achieved rows in the top two thirds.

music.notes: Warm acoustic guitar or felt piano. It should feel like a quiet pat on the back, not a sad montage. Steady through the list.

creatives.name: Tip 3: on a good day, do half
creatives.title: POTS tip #3: on a good day, do half
creatives.goal: Third single tip. The pacing one, and the most natural lead into the app.
creatives.caption: POTS tip #3, and the one that took me longest to learn 🩵 Good days are where crashes are made. #pots #pacing #mecfs #longcovid #dysautonomia

text: POTS tip #3:
On a good day, *do half* of what you think you can.

img.search: to do list notebook half crossed off
img.shows: A handwritten to-do list with only the first few items crossed off.
img.frame: List in the lower half; the tip in the space above.

text: A good day feels like a chance to catch up.
*That's the trap.* The bill shows up two days later.

img.shows: A half-finished chore: boxes in a garage, a mower on a half-cut lawn. No people.
img.frame: The unfinished job in the top half; copy over the lower half.

text: So I let my numbers set the limit, *not my mood.*
The app I built gives me a daily pacing budget. Link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home: Outlook card and the pacing strip, 1h 21m left of 3h 35m, ahead of pace.
img.frame: Pacing strip level with the copy.

music.notes: Same sound family as tips #1 and #2. A touch more thoughtful on slide 2, where the trap lands.

creatives.name: My morning routine, as a dad with POTS
creatives.title: My morning routine as a dad with POTS ☀️
creatives.goal: Routine format with a punchline, and the app shown doing its actual job.
creatives.caption: Step 5 is not optional and not up to me 😂🩵 #pots #potsdad #morningroutine #dysautonomia #hrv

text: My morning routine as *a dad with POTS.*

img.shows: You in bed, just awake, hair a mess, squinting at the camera.
img.frame: Face in the upper third, pillow and blanket in frame. Morning light.

text: 1. Wake up. Do not stand up.
2. Water and salt, still in bed
3. HRV reading before anything else
4. Stand up like I'm defusing a bomb
5. Kids have been up for an hour

img.shows: Rumpled sheets in morning light. No people.
img.frame: Darkened about 85% under the list.

text: Step 3 takes a few minutes and tells me *what kind of day it's going to be.*

img.shows: Progress, HRV section: the daily RMSSD line with the 'Healthy 38 year old men' range under it.
img.frame: HRV chart beside the copy.

text: Then I know how much dad *I've got today.*
Free app I built, link in bio. 🩵

img.shows: The Journal home: Outlook card with the score, pacing strip, HRV / resting HR / sleep tiles.
img.frame: Full-height screenshot from the top.

music.notes: The classic upbeat 'that girl' morning routine sound, played against a routine where step one is not standing up. Keep it bouncy all the way through.
